convention_compliance.workflow_naming: deviation: 'license_application_carrier_side' uses descriptive snake_case rather than the recommended <Verb>By<Role> pattern (e.g., 'LicenseAppliedForByCarrier'). Recommended fix: rename to 'license_applied_for_by_carrier' on next minor version.

author_intent_notes:
Worked example produced via the micro-app-template-gen skill on 2026-05-11 as the capstone proof that spec + toolchain + skill are coherent end-to-end; migrated to CEL/1.0 on 2026-07-13 (Stage 3 of the expression-language migration, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-13-uel-cel-migration.md). Authoring scenario: startup carrier (no imported credentials initially) applies to a state regulator for an insurance license; pivotal event is 'an application has been submitted and adjudicated'. The carrier exports nothing in this micro-app — they only receive. The regulator's complementary side is the separate regulator-grants-carrier-license template.

Note on credential imports: although the carrier starts with no active license instance, the schema requires that credential types referenced by reactions and workflows be declared in credentials.imports. The 'carrier_license' entry is therefore a type declaration, not an active-instance assertion. Its expected_schema_said was marked TBD at authoring time pending alignment with the regulator's exported-credential schema (superseded at v1.1 — now pinned to the regulator's carrier_license schema SAID; see the v1.1 re-model note below).

CEL/1.0 expressions are written against the bound-context cheat-sheet (references/cel-1.0-cheat-sheet.md). As part of the 2026-07-13 migration every expression in this template was compile-checked against cel-python 0.5.0 (the pinned CEL/1.0 runtime evaluator), and every test_vectors entry was executed through a reference fold engine implementing the accepted spec's reference semantics (ugard docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-cel-declarative-aggregates-and-projections.md §11) — all vectors reproduce their declared expected state. Notable expression decisions:
  - no_active_license_for_jurisdiction (state precondition) is rewritten from the earlier arrow-lambda .filter/.length idiom to CEL's .filter(x, ...)/size(...), and the stray command.payload.jurisdiction nesting is corrected to command.jurisdiction (state_precondition binds { state, command, principal } directly over the command's payload_schema fields — no .payload. nesting, per the cheat-sheet's bound-context table). The same bound-context fix applies to submit_application's aggregate_event payload_mapping: bare payload.jurisdiction/payload.lines_of_business references are corrected to command.* (command emissions bind { command, state }; there is no 'payload' variable in scope).
  - All map literals in every expression use quoted string keys ({ "jurisdiction": command.jurisdiction }, never { jurisdiction: ... }): CEL map-literal keys are expressions, so a bare identifier key evaluates as an unbound variable — verified failure on cel-python 0.5.0.
  - no_duplicate_active_license_per_jurisdiction (aggregate invariant) is rewritten from .every/.filter/.length to CEL's .all(x, ...)/.filter(x, ...)/size(...).
  - license_terms_acceptable (workflow branch condition) is rewritten from the earlier arrow-lambda .every/.includes idiom to CEL's .all(l, ...) plus the 'in' membership operator (CEL has no .includes()/.contains() on lists; cheat-sheet §8 gotcha).
  - The aggregate now carries an explicit fold handler map (template spec §6.5), replacing the earlier absent fold: application_submitted is an op-list append; license_granted and license_revoked are raw reducers because they touch two arrays at once (marking the matching application's status while adding/removing the corresponding active_licenses row) and the object-state op vocabulary (set/append/remove/increment/merge/move) has no single op for that. boundary.instance_key is a constant ('license_registry') because this aggregate is the carrier's own single private registry, not partitioned by any event field.
  - my_active_licenses projection is migrated to shape: "collection" with primary_key: "license_said", an explicit fold handler map (upsert on grant, delete on revoke), and ordering: "source_seq" (single log). output_schema is renamed row_schema per the amended template spec.
  - idempotency_key_expression is removed from submit_application: the field was dropped from the template spec during canon consolidation (THE DECISION §3.6 amendment 4; the runtime dedups on the exn message's SAID instead), and its old expression (hash(...)/.sort()/.join()) was not valid CEL regardless.

Adversarial review performed 2026-05-11; re-reviewed 2026-07-13 for the CEL/1.0 migration. Walked checklist items 1-10. Identified concerns:
  1. Impersonation: state_preconditions reference the license_registry aggregate but submit_application has no auth_preconditions because the carrier is by definition the principal — KERI signature on the outbound exn establishes identity. Acceptable.
  2. Credential revocation timing: the on_license_revoked reaction folds revocation events; the my_active_licenses projection's delete-on-license_revoked handler excludes revoked licenses. Acceptable.
  3. Concurrent commands: two submit_application commands for the same jurisdiction would both pass the precondition at command time if state were stale; the aggregate invariant catches the resulting duplicate. The loser's UI experience is undefined and worth surfacing.
  4. Missed events: my_active_licenses now folds via explicit upsert/delete handlers (idempotent by construction). Acceptable.
  5. Counterparty bad behavior: step_await_decision has time_bound P90D and expected_inbound covers both grant and explicit denial. Acceptable.
  6. Compromised actor keys: KERI rotation semantics apply; aggregate respects key state at command time. Acceptable for licensing.
  7. Schema versioning: not exercised in this micro-app (no exported credentials).
  8. Convention divergence: workflow id deviation documented above.
  9. Idempotency under network retry: this template has no idempotency_key_expression (field removed from the spec); the runtime dedups on the exn message's SAID instead.
  10. Permission escalation: not exercised (no exported credentials).

Stage 3b (final whole-range review, 2026-07-14) fixed three cross-stage coherence defects surfaced by the post-Stage-5 review, all re-verified by execution (not just compile-check): my_active_licenses' row_schema carried a legacy whole-table wrapper ({ properties: { rows: { items: <row>, type: array } } }); per template spec §6.8, row_schema is JSON-Schema for ONE ROW, so it was reshaped to the bare per-row object schema (no rows wrapper) — this also cleared spurious "not in schema" hints the Designer's field-picker was firing against this projection's upsert set-field editor. Separately, submit_application's aggregate_event payload_mapping referenced event.timestamp for submitted_at, but a command emission's payload_mapping binds only {command, state} (cheat-sheet §2) — no event exists at emission time. submitted_at is genuinely consumed (state_schema-required on applications, read by the aggregate fold's application_submitted append and by license_granted's application-status-flip, test-vector-asserted), so it was promoted to a required, client-supplied field on submit_application's payload_schema (date-time; the Locksmith UI is expected to auto-fill the client clock at send time), and payload_mapping now reads command.submitted_at. This changes only payload_schema/payload_mapping — the fold handler and test_vectors already read event.submitted_at and already supplied the literal value directly in each vector's event.payload, so neither needed to change. Finally, both reactions (on_license_granted: credential_received; on_license_revoked: lifecycle_event) used bare credential.d/credential.attributes.* where the cheat-sheet's bound name is event.credential.* — and credential.d specifically is doubly wrong, since the bound event.credential shape (cheat-sheet §2 Shapes) exposes said, not d (an ACDC/KERI-ism with no CEL binding), so it was rewritten to event.credential.said, not just re-prefixed. event.timestamp in both reactions became event.datetime (event genuinely exists for both trigger types; only the field name was stale). Note for the owner: on_license_revoked's trigger is lifecycle_event, not credential_received; the cheat-sheet's §2 Shapes table annotates event.credential as available "(reactions on credential_received only)" and does not separately document a credential-access path for lifecycle_event. Since license_said is the only field this reaction's fold actually consumes (jurisdiction is read from existing state, not the event, per the aggregate's license_revoked reducer) and there is no other documented source for the transitioning credential's identity, event.credential.said was applied to both reactions on the reasoning that a lifecycle_event about a specific credential instance must expose that credential somehow and this is the only sanctioned shape for it — not a new binding, but an application of an existing one slightly beyond its literally-annotated scope. Flagged rather than silently assumed safe; recommend the cheat-sheet's §2 table be extended to state this explicitly. Every rewritten expression was evaluated — not just compiled — against cel-python 0.5.0 with a stub context supplying that slot's exact bound variables, per the same reference-fold-engine method Stage 3 used; all pre-existing test_vectors were re-run and still reproduce their declared expected state unchanged. (A fourth, unrelated bare-credential reference was found in this template's license_terms_acceptable rule, purpose workflow_branch_condition — out of this fix's scope, since FIX 2 covers payload_mapping/reaction expressions specifically and workflow_branch_condition's bound context, {state, command, workflow, principal} per cheat-sheet §2, has no credential slot at all, documented or otherwise; flagged separately for the owner rather than guessed at.)

Open risks: the aggregate's license_granted fold reducer flips EVERY pending application whose jurisdiction matches the grant to status 'granted' in one step (the aggregate has no application_id concept, so jurisdiction + status == 'pending' is the entire correlation key — this is not a tie-break that might pick a wrong row, it is a bulk update of all matching rows). With two simultaneous pending applications for the same jurisdiction (already discouraged in practice by no_active_license_for_jurisdiction, but not prevented by any application-level uniqueness rule), one grant would mark both applications granted. license_revoked has the narrower analog via its license_said match. An application_id on the payload schema (and in the fold's correlation) is the fix; deferred to a future revision. The three CEL expressions inherited from the pre-migration best-effort authoring (no_active_license_for_jurisdiction, no_duplicate_active_license_per_jurisdiction, license_terms_acceptable) remain otherwise unreviewed beyond this migration's syntax/idiom correction.

v1.1 re-model (2026-07-15, promoted from the lmad skill example into ugard's canonical docs/micro-apps/ location as part of the carrier-license-application schema work, Task 3 of that effort): the carrier's application is re-modeled from a transient, null-credential IPEX 'apply' exn into a self-issued ACDC (schema carrier_license_application, SAID ENbhxLlFINUDp1EU4mV5RVVL-CS6Ub72zXY89EcM7Ccb, issuer == issuee == the carrier) presented to the state-doi via IPEX 'grant', mirroring the shape the regulator-side template already used for its own exported carrier_license credential (exchange + lifecycle_advance + aggregate_event, in that order). This resolves the 'Open risks' application_id gap noted above at the correlation-key level for future work: the newly self-issued application now carries its own SAID (application_said), which is carried on the emitted application_submitted event via runtime enrichment — NOT via the command's payload_mapping. This matches the ecosystem convention the sibling regulator-grants-carrier-license template establishes: its grant_license aggregate_event payload_mapping does not reference command.license_said, yet the license_granted fold reads event.license_said — the runtime enriches the emitted event with the issued credential's SAID after payload_mapping. Here, submit_application's application_submitted payload_mapping deliberately omits application_said (it binds only { command, state }, and the self-issued application's SAID is computed by the exchange/lifecycle_advance issuance step of this same command, so it is not available to the command-scope mapping); the runtime enriches the emitted application_submitted event with the self-issued application ACDC's SAID, exactly as the DOI's grant enriches license_granted with license_said. The SAID is then threaded through the license_registry aggregate's applications rows (state_schema requires application_said, the application_submitted append fold step reads event.application_said, and the license_granted raw-reducer's per-row map carries application_said forward on every jurisdiction-matched row it rewrites — which would otherwise have dropped the now-required field) — a real, addressable correlation key is available where before there was none, though the license_granted reducer itself still matches by jurisdiction+status rather than by application_said, so the bulk-update behavior described above is unchanged by this revision and remains the deferred fix. The carrier_license import's expected_schema_said is pinned to LICENSE_SCHEMA_SAID (ENIhMZdlSsMGOw7qMkE8VHcSS9RdEC1-aBom-R9cX42x, produced by the sibling regulator-side effort), and its narrative's 'TBD until the regulator's micro-app fixes it' clause is dropped accordingly. submit_application's lines_of_business enum is harmonized to the license schema's set (retiring workers_comp in favor of workers_compensation, and adding casualty, marine, aviation), and a representations object (solvency_reserves_usd, solvency_attestation required; naic_number, years_in_operation optional) is added to match the credential schema's attributes block — both submit_application's payload_schema and the exported credential's attributes are now the same shape. application_said is NOT a payload_schema field at all (it is not client input); it is carried on the emitted event via runtime enrichment as described above, consistent with the sibling regulator-grants-carrier-license license_granted/license_said pattern.
